name: Isolated Focal Non-Epidermolytic Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Focal Non-Epidermolytic Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated, localized hyperkeratotic plaques on pressure-bearing areas of palms and/or soles
Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis without epidermolytic changes
Exclusion of epidermolytic and other syndromic palmoplantar keratodermas by clinical and histological evaluation
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance (supportive but not required)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: clinical presentation, histopathology without epidermolytic changes, and exclusion of other keratoderma types.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be inconclusive; diagnosis primarily clinical and histopathological.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized hyperkeratotic plaques on pressure points of palms and soles
searchTerms: thickened skin patches on palms and soles
hard skin spots on pressure areas of hands and feet
localized rough skin on palms and soles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of epidermolytic changes on histopathology
searchTerms: no skin blistering changes on pathology
absence of epidermal breakdown under microscope
painful cracks in thickened skin plaques
painful skin fissures in hardened areas
cracked painful skin in thick plaques

common.symptomName: Callus formation on weight-bearing areas of soles
searchTerms: thickened skin on soles from pressure
foot callus formation under pressure points
mild redness around thickened skin lesions

common.symptomName: Thickened skin texture localized to focal areas

occasional.notes: Usually due to skin barrier disruption

searchTerms: excessive sweating on hands and feet
overactive sweat glands in hands and feet
damaged nails next to skin spots

rare.symptomName: Development of painful blisters secondary to mechanical trauma
Extension of hyperkeratosis beyond focal areas

searchTerms: slight increased sensitivity in hands and feet

laboratory: Negative fungal cultures to exclude tinea
other: Histopathology showing hyperkeratosis without epidermolytic changes

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of epidermolytic changes on histopathology
More diffuse involvement of palms and soles
Often associated with blistering in infancy
Multiple small hyperkeratotic papules rather than focal plaques
Histopathology shows epidermolytic or non-epidermolytic changes depending on subtype
Usually autosomal dominant inheritance with distinct clinical pattern

redFlags: Rapid progression of lesions beyond focal areas
Development of painful blistering or ulceration
Signs of secondary infection such as purulence or systemic symptoms
